notes: EIGHT BLOCKS AND NO code_section. This page has eight `sections` rows — why, what,
implants, process, types, candidacy, gallery, faq — in exactly the order of its eight
template bands, and it mounts no <LocalTrust> and no other bespoke component band, so
there is nothing for the escape hatch to hold a place for. That is the first structural
difference from all three migrated cosmetic routes, and it is why `exempt.toc_links` can
be empty without a code_section claiming an anchor.
BAND VOCABULARY IS THE PILOT'S ON THIS PAGE — AND THE TEMPLATE'S OWN BAND COMMENTS SAID
OTHERWISE. `.bgraft .section.alt` is CHARCOAL (bone-grafting.css:227 ->
var(--vs-charcoal-green), with h1-h4 #fff at :228-231 and p rgba(255,255,255,0.85) at
:235) and `.bgraft .section.dark` is SAGE-PALE (bone-grafting.css:237 ->
var(--vs-sage-pale), with h1-h4 var(--vs-ink) at :238-241). Before this migration the
file's own comments called `what` and `candidacy` "cream" and `process` "sage" — three
wrong band values sitting one line above the markup they describe. Every `band` below is
read off the RULE, and `band_evidence` names it; a reviewer who trusts the comments
repaints four of these eight bands.
THIS PAGE HAS `cards` ROWS, IN THREE GROUPS, AND TWO OF THE THREE ARE MOVED. Verified
live: whyCards (4 rows, meta 01-04), procedures (3 rows, meta "Procedure"), materials
(3 rows, meta Allograft/Xenograft/Synthetic). whyCards fills the `why` card grid and
procedures fills the `types` comparison cards. The three `materials` rows have no
layout that draws them and are listed in `exempt.cards` — they are the only rows on
this page that a backfill leaves behind, and they are real CMS content, not template
copy.
THIS ROUTE LOSES MORE THAN EITHER WORKED EXAMPLE, AND THE LOSSES ARE THE THREE
ADAPTATIONS THE FILE HEADER LISTS (bone-grafting.astro:6-15). `.what-causes`, the whole
`.implants-intro` + `.implants-band` restructure, the `.materials-block` <dl>, and
`.candidacy-sub` have no field on any of the nine registered layouts. Each is named in
`known_gaps` on the block it belongs to, with the copy quoted verbatim so it is
recoverable from this file alone, and with what would close it.
WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: relocate template copy into a field that draws

different markup. `.what-causes` and `.candidacy-sub` are both an

over a

and
media_split's callout pair would carry those two elements — but the callout draws
<aside class="veneers-callout"> and draws it INSIDE `.natural-text`, where
`.candidacy-sub` is a full-width card BELOW `.natural-grid`. Filling those fields would
produce a page that looks migrated and is not the page this map is verified against,
which is the trade the teeth-whitening route refused for its nested price table. A
recorded gap is visible; a relocated element is not.
THIS IS THE FIRST ROUTE TO STORE card_grid `columns: "4"`, and it exposes a breakpoint
the three cosmetic routes could not. `.bgraft .why-grid` collapses to two tracks at
1240px (bone-grafting.css:854-856), but that rule is (0,2,0) while CardGridBlock's
scoped `.why-grid.cols-4` is (0,3,0) and a media query adds no specificity — so the
backfilled band draws FOUR across between 992px and 1240px where the page draws two.
See `known_gaps` on the `why` block. Nothing in this file can fix it and no additive
page-sheet rule can either: a `.bgraft .why-grid.cols-4` override is also (0,3,0) and
ties, which is decided by bundle order.
ONE PRE-EXISTING FAMILY CONDITION, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT READ AS THIS ROUTE'S. This
sheet stacks `.what-grid`, `.natural-grid` and `.compare` at 1100px (bone-grafting.css:
864-868) where MediaSplitBlock and ComparisonCardsBlock stack at 991px
(MediaSplitBlock.astro:934, ComparisonCardsBlock.astro:581). Both sides are (0,2,0) —
the page's `.bgraft .what-grid` and the block's scoped `.what-grid` — so the 992-1100px
band is settled by bundle order. porcelain-veneers.css:651-660 has the identical shape,
so this is the family's condition and not a difference this migration introduces.

No `lead` is mapped and none exists to map. The template's .why-card is a .num, an

and ONE

cards.meta_is_not_moved: The four rows carry meta "01" through "04" and it is deliberately NOT mapped. `numbered` above makes CardGridBlock derive the figure from row position (CardGridBlock.astro:146-150), which yields the same four strings and cannot fall out of sequence when an editor reorders the grid. figure() reads `meta` only when `numbered` is false, so the stored values are simply unused rather than in conflict.

known_gaps: ONE, AND IT IS A BREAKPOINT RATHER THAN A FIELD.
Every element of this band has a field: the head is the CMS `why` row, the four cards
are the CMS whyCards rows, and the numbering is derived. Nothing about the content is
lost.
WHAT IS LOST IS THE 1240px COLLAPSE. This sheet narrows .why-grid to two tracks at
1240px (bone-grafting.css:854-856) — a rule at (0,2,0). CardGridBlock's scoped
`.why-grid.cols-4` is (0,3,0) and its own breakpoints start at 991px
(CardGridBlock.astro:407-419), and a media query contributes no specificity, so the
four-track declaration wins INSIDE this page's own 1240px query. Between 992px and
1240px the backfilled band draws four 18px-gutter cards across a viewport that draws
two today. This is the first route to emit `.cols-4` at all — the three cosmetic
routes all store "2" and never reach the compound — so nothing has hit it before.
WHAT CLOSES IT is a `@media (max-width: 1240px)` rule for `.why-grid.cols-4` in
CardGridBlock.astro, alongside the 991px and 780px blocks it already has. It cannot be
closed from this file, and it cannot be closed from bone-grafting.css either: a
`.bgraft .why-grid.cols-4` override is also (0,3,0), which ties with the scoped
compound and is settled by whichever stylesheet the bundler emits last. Exactly the
specificity trap ProcessStepsBlock.astro:496-530 documents for `.cols-5`, one
breakpoint further out.

known_gaps: TWO. ONE IS A HOVER LABEL; THE OTHER IS A WHOLE SUB-BLOCK.
THE HOVER LABEL, and it is a component fact rather than a missing field.
MediaSplitBlock reads each button's hover label from CTA_HOVER, a table keyed by HREF
(MediaSplitBlock.astro:233-238), and "#process" maps to "View Steps" — which is not
what this template passes: bone-grafting.astro:386 passes hoverLabel="See How". So the
second button returns with data-hover="View Steps" and "View Steps" in its .l2 span.
Visible only on hover, and there is no value this map could supply: one href cannot
carry two labels, so closing it means a hover-label sub-field on the layout or a
per-band override in the component. The teeth-whitening route carries the identical
residue for the identical reason ("View Levels").
THE `.what-causes` SUB-BLOCK IS LOST WHOLE — bone-grafting.astro:369-374, sitting
between .prose and .cta-row inside .what-text. It is four elements:
(a 56px sage hairline, bone-grafting.css:923-929)
Causes
Why Jawbone Loss Happens

Jawbone loss most often results from tooth extraction without replacement, periodontal disease, or a missing tooth left untreated for years. How quickly bone resorbs varies by patient. CBCT imaging reveals your current bone volume and determines whether grafting is necessary before implant planning begins.
None of it is in the CMS, so a backfilled page shows no causes content at all and the
page's own header note (bone-grafting.astro:12-14) describes a layout the page no
longer has.
NOT FILLED INTO `callout_heading` / `callout_body`, deliberately. That pair draws
<aside class="veneers-callout"> (MediaSplitBlock.astro:445-455) — a different element,
a different class, no eyebrow and no rule div — and this sheet styles
`.bgraft .what-causes h3` and `.bgraft .what-text .what-causes + .cta-row`
(bone-grafting.css:933-950), neither of which would match. It would put the words back
in roughly the right place wearing the wrong markup, which the governing rule at the
top of block-map.json rules out.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT is either (a) a `causes_*` field group on media_split plus the
`.what-causes` markup in MediaSplitBlock — a bespoke shape for one band, which is the
trade manifest.ts warns against — or (b) restyling `.what-causes` as a
`.veneers-callout` in this page's own markup FIRST, so the existing callout pair fits
with no new field. (b) is the same move teeth-whitening's price-table gap asks for and
is the cheaper of the two.

known_gaps: THE LARGEST SHAPE LOSS ON THIS ROUTE, AND THE ONE THE PAGE WAS EXPLICITLY BUILT TO
AVOID.
WHAT SURVIVES: the CMS `implants` row (eyebrow "Grafting & Implants", heading
"Bone Grafting and Dental Implants", and its paragraph) and the implantsImg
photo with its alt.
WHAT IS LOST IS THE STRUCTURE. The template stacks a centred .implants-intro
(max-width 760px, text-align center, bone-grafting.css:1043-1052) over a sage-tinted
asymmetric .implants-band card. media_split returns all of it as one .what-grid split
with .what-img beside .what-text — which is the 50/50 shape sitting directly above it
in #what, and which bone-grafting.astro:271-277 says in as many words was restructured

WHAT IS LOST AS COPY is the whole .implants-band-text, bone-grafting.astro:436-450,
none of it in the CMS:
Why grafting comes first
Foundation, then placement.

Bone grafting is needed when bone loss is significant enough to prevent stable implant placement. Common candidates include patients with unpreserved extraction sites, multiple missing teeth, or denture wearers considering implant-supported options. Not all implant cases require grafting, and a CBCT evaluation at Vivid Smiles confirms whether it applies to you.
That paragraph carries this page's ONLY two internal links, to
/implant-dentistry/single-tooth-dental-implants/ and
/implant-dentistry/full-mouth-dental-implants/. A backfilled page links to neither.
NOT FILLED INTO `body_2`, deliberately, even though body_2 is html-bearing and would
carry both anchors (MediaSplitBlock.astro:327, 469-473). body_2 draws a second
INSIDE .prose, and this paragraph is not a second prose paragraph — it is the body of
a separate card with its own eyebrow and <h3>. Same refusal as `.what-causes` above,
and for the same reason.
ONE SMALLER DIFFERENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD AS A BUG: the parallax depth.
The template gives .implants-band-img data-parallax="-15" (bone-grafting.astro:428);
MediaSplitBlock hardcodes -25 on its .what-img (MediaSplitBlock.astro:405). No field
carries it.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: this band is a candidate for `code_section`, not for a new
media_split field. It is one bespoke shape used once, its copy is entirely
hardcoded, and code_section exists exactly so such a band keeps a POSITION in the
ordered list without becoming editable — which is the whole difference between
"stays in code" and "cannot be positioned". Doing that means lifting
bone-grafting.astro:419-453 into a component, one entry in CodeSectionBlock.astro's
BANDS map and one choice `bone_grafting_implants` in BLOCK_CODE_BANDS
(vs-content-model.php), in the same commit — miss either side and the row writes
cleanly, resolves to nothing, and the band vanishes with a console warning as the only
trace. It would also change what `exempt` says: the implantsImg row and the `implants`
sections row would then be unclaimed and would have to move here.

known_gaps: TWO, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONLY PLACE ON THIS ROUTE WHERE LIVE CMS ROWS GO
UNRENDERED.
ONE — THE CARD MARKUP IS RENAMED. The template draws these three as
<div class="alternatives-grid"> of <article class="config-card"> with a <span

class="tag">, an

and a

(bone-grafting.astro:529-539).
ComparisonCardsBlock draws <div class="compare"> of <article class="compare-card">

with the same , an

and a

. So the grid class, the card class
and one heading level all change. The rendered columns happen to agree at desktop —
.bgraft .alternatives-grid is repeat(3, 1fr) (bone-grafting.css:530-532) and the
block's .compare is three across — but .bgraft .config-card's own type scale
(bone-grafting.css:374-394) stops matching, because no .config-card exists to match
it. What would close it is markup, not a field: renaming this band's grid and cards to
.compare / .compare-card and its <h4> to an <h3> in the .astro makes it the shape the
layout already draws, and needs nothing new anywhere.
TWO — THE ENTIRE .materials-block IS LOST, bone-grafting.astro:545-564, and its three
definitions are CMS rows rather than template copy:
<div class="materials-head">
Material Sources
Where Does Bone Graft Material Come From?
Graft material is selected based on your anatomy and the procedure required.
<dl class="materials-list"> — three .material-row, each a <dt> of <span class="tag">
plus <span class="label">, and a <dd>:
Allograft / Processed donor bone / "Processed donor bone from a certified tissue bank; integrates predictably with natural jawbone."
Xenograft / Bovine-derived mineral / "Mineral derived from bovine bone, used for its structural compatibility with human jaw tissue."
Synthetic / Lab-made scaffold / "Lab-made scaffold material that supports new bone growth while your body rebuilds around it."
Those three are the live `cards` group `materials` (meta / title / body), which is why

and

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `definitions` repeater on comparison_cards (term / label /
body) plus the <dl> markup in ComparisonCardsBlock — and the name must be checked
against every repeater already in `blocks` before it is minted, because `items`,

are taken and a collision merges two types silently. The cheaper alternative is a
second block: split the materials into their own <section> so a card_grid or a future
glossary layout can hold it — but that mints a new anchor and a new rail entry, and
the seven toc_links rows do not have one.

literal.item: Patients whose teeth were removed without a socket-preservation graft at the time of extraction.
When several teeth have been absent long enough for surrounding bone to resorb.
Long-term denture wear accelerates bone loss; grafting often restores enough volume to switch to an implant-supported option.
Not all implant cases require grafting, and a CBCT evaluation at Vivid Smiles confirms whether it applies to you.

known_gaps: ONE, AND IT TAKES A LIVE CMS PARAGRAPH WITH IT.
THE `.candidacy-sub` CARD IS LOST — bone-grafting.astro:636-640, a full-width 940px
white card with a 3px sage left border sitting BELOW .natural-grid inside the same
.wrap (bone-grafting.css:575-599). Three elements:
The bottom line
An imaging-guided foundation for implants
{section("candidacy").body}
The first two are hardcoded. The third is the LIVE `candidacy` row's body — "Bone
grafting makes implant placement possible for patients who have experienced
significant jawbone loss, and Dr. Richardson's imaging-guided approach ensures every
decision is based on your actual anatomy. Understanding the timeline and your
candidacy removes the uncertainty that often delays treatment." — which is why `body`
above is blank rather than mapped: the paragraph exists in the CMS and there is
nowhere on this layout it can render where the page puts it.
NOT FILLED INTO `callout_heading` / `callout_body`. Those draw
<aside class="veneers-callout"> INSIDE .natural-text (MediaSplitBlock.astro:445-455),
i.e. inside the left column of a two-column grid, where .candidacy-sub is a centred
card below the whole grid. The element, the class and the position all differ and the
.label would still be lost, so filling them would relocate a card rather than
reproduce it.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the shape is a labelled closing card, and three implant pages in
this family carry something like it — worth checking before inventing anything. If it
is genuinely one-off, the cheap close is markup: fold the <h3> and the paragraph into
the existing .natural-text column as a `.veneers-callout` in the .astro first, and the
deployed callout pair then carries them with no new field. The expensive close is a
`closing_card` group on media_split drawn after the grid, which is a new position in
the component as well as new fields.

types, candidacy, faq — are claimed by a block above on its `section_id`. There is no
code_section on this route, so unlike all three cosmetic pages no anchor is claimed any
The rail is derived from blocks[].anchor + nav_label in block order. Eight blocks
produce 7 rail entries — `gallery` has no toc_links row and stays out — in the order
Why Vivid Smiles, What It Is, Grafting & Implants, The Procedure, Types & Materials,
Who Needs It, FAQ, which is the order the template build puts them in. So the rail is
not a difference on this route.
TWO RAIL LABELS PROMISE MORE THAN THE BACKFILLED BAND DELIVERS, and that is worth
seeing next to the gaps rather than only inside them. "Grafting & Implants" scrolls to
a band that has lost its .implants-band card and both of the page's internal links, and
"Types & Materials" scrolls to a band that has lost every material. Neither link
breaks; both under-deliver until the two gaps close.
